triggers.when: "before a feature-labelled commit, or when reading someone else's branch"
triggers.say: This is a feature-labelled commit or someone else's branch. diff-review separates must-fix from nice-to-have and hunts swallowed failures.

triggers.when: "changing a package manager or its version, adding a packageManager field, moving a build-script allow-list"
triggers.say: A package manager or dependency manifest is changing. Pin the version and prefer a digest; an unpinned manager is how a CI install starts failing for reasons unrelated to the change being made.

triggers.when: "adding or updating any dependency - a package, a native library, a build flag that changes what links, an AI model, a font or asset, a vendored source tree, a base image"
triggers.say: A dependency manifest or build definition is changing. Before it lands, check the licence of everything the built artefacts now load, not just the package chosen; anything copyleft, GPL-with-exception, non-commercial or custom goes to the owner first.

triggers.when: "building or reviewing any loop, batch job, reconciliation or scheduled automation, and whenever a run succeeded but the expected side effect is missing"
triggers.say: Scheduled or batch work: check item COUNTS, not exit status. A job that finishes green may have processed nothing.

triggers.when: "writing a runbook, checklist or deploy step, or about to run an action that can interrupt the live product: a firewall reload, a container or daemon restart, a DNS, tunnel or access change, a live workflow publish, a migration on live tables, a deploy that serves traffic"
triggers.say: A step that can touch the live product says what it affects, for how long and whether it needs a quiet window, and is verified from outside afterwards. Firewall reloads, restarts, tunnel and DNS changes, live workflow publishes and live-table migrations always get the note.

triggers.when: "before writing any product claim, price, launch status, platform or integration list, compliance or security assertion, legal and policy text, competitor comparison, or biographical fact"
triggers.say: This page carries claims no amount of searching the repo can settle -- price, compliance, competitor or biographical fact. Those are the owner's to decide, not mine to infer.

triggers.when: "writing or editing user-facing copy - headlines, feature blurbs, marketing pages, product descriptions, release notes"
triggers.say: User-facing copy. Write it once and reference it -- the same sentence, address or URL typed into a second file is the thing that later drifts.

triggers.when: the file that tells every future session how to work in this repo
triggers.say: Editing the repo's agent instructions. Format and placement decide whether later sessions actually read this.

triggers.when: PowerShell and Windows-specific behaviour that silently differs
triggers.say: A PowerShell script. 5.1 has no && or ternary, native stderr redirection fakes failures, and Set-Content defaults to ANSI.

triggers.when: opening a pull request, or pushing a branch that will become one
triggers.say: Opening a PR. The gates only run on the PR, so what lands here is what reviewers and CI actually see.

triggers.when: a merge is not a deploy, and green CI is not a running service
triggers.say: Merging is not shipping. Confirm the thing is actually running where users are before calling it done.

triggers.when: "an alert nobody reads is not an alert"
triggers.say: Alert configuration. Every alert needs a destination scoped to the product and environment it belongs to.

triggers.when: release automation that succeeds while shipping nothing
triggers.say: A release workflow. These fail in ways that still report green.

triggers.when: utility classes losing to un-layered CSS
triggers.say: Tailwind config. Un-layered custom CSS silently outranks utilities.

triggers.when: checking a credential's configuration without revealing its value
triggers.say: Inspect a secret's shape, never its value. Check config indirectly rather than decoding .data.

triggers.when: "writing an HTML page or a report-shaped Markdown file for someone to read"
triggers.say: This looks like an answer someone will read. report-pages: start from its template, answer first, a verdict per item, readable on a phone; publish it so answers come back to you instead of as prose.

triggers.when: "before creating a folder outside the current repo - a worktree, a clone, QA or test data ... whenever a command would create a folder at a drive root, in the home folder or directly in the projects folder"
triggers.say: A folder is being made outside the repo. folder-placement: worktrees go in the harness's worktree folder or <repo>.worktrees/<task>, scratch and QA data in the scratch root via make_scratch.py, never at a drive root, and every folder gets a label so cleanup can tell it from the user's own.

triggers.when: "removing local folders, clones or worktrees, running git worktree remove or prune, deleting a scratch or QA data folder, freeing disk space"
triggers.say: Something local is being removed. local-cleanup: inventory first, act only on what the user marked, and move to holding (restorable) instead of deleting; never --force past a refusal.

triggers.when: "the user says the disk is full, messy ... asks which local folders, clones or worktrees are still needed"
triggers.say: Folder sizes are being measured. local-compare: local_inventory.py lists every clone, worktree and folder with its branch, unpushed and merge state, size and a safe / review / keep verdict, in one pass.

triggers.when: "before writing or editing a personal.toml profile or Gnomonkit's onboarding.json by hand"
triggers.say: A Gnomonkit profile file is being written by hand. onboarding: save values with `gnomonkit profile set key=value`, which checks each one, keeps a .bak copy and writes nothing when a value is wrong.

triggers.when: "before writing a gnomonkit-overlay.toml marker or an overlay's marketplace by hand"
triggers.say: A Gnomonkit overlay marker is being written by hand. overlay-setup: `gnomonkit overlay init` or `convert --apply` writes the marker and the manifests together, and `gnomonkit overlay check` validates the layout.
